- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecasts are flat or trending down, adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to account for sentiment-driven momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior period), model tends to overcorrect downward; reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.5% per subsequent period to avoid overshoot.
- In high-event periods (≥15 events/30d), model overestimates mean price; apply downward bias of 2–5% to offset supply-driven volatility.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and model forecasts are rising, reverse trend by 0.5–1.0% per period to avoid false bullishness.
- In low-event periods (≤5 events/30d), model underestimates volatility; add 0.5–1.5% noise to forecast to reflect sentiment lag.
- When supply net is negative and bullish sentiment is low, model underestimates price; add 1–2% upward bias to reflect policy-driven support.
- In multi-period auction cycles (e.g., CAP3 EU/DE), model tends to overpredict early periods; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for first 3–5 periods after auction.
